title: Sync Status in Your WordPress Dashboard
summary: Whalesync Status is a small WordPress plugin that shows each post’s sync status in WP admin and adds a Sync now button to the edit screen.
body_markdown:
We made a small WordPress plugin. It’s called[Whalesync Status](https://wordpress.org/plugins/whalesync/) , and it’s in the WordPress plugin directory today.


Our[WordPress connector](https://www.whalesync.com/connector/wordpress) syncs your posts and pages with Airtable, Notion, Google Sheets, and the rest without anything installed on your site. The plugin isn't a required part of syncing with Whalesync, but it makes the experience a bit nicer. It lets your whole team see what the sync has been up to inside your dashboard, without opening Whalesync.


## **What it adds**


- **A status column** in your posts list, so each synced post says what last happened to it: “Updated from Airtable · 5 minutes ago”. Pages and custom post types get it too, if your sync maps them.
- **A banner on the edit screen** , so whoever opens a post knows it’s being synced by Whalesync, with a **Sync now** button for when you don’t want to wait.
- **A sync overview** under Settings → Whalesync Status, with any issues or pending deletes that need someone to look at them.


The Whalesync status column in the posts list


## **Getting set up**


1. In WP admin, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Whalesync”, and install and activate it.
2. Open Settings → Whalesync Status and click **Connect with Whalesync** .
3. Sign in, pick your sync, and approve.


It’s version 1.0 and pretty small on purpose. If you find it useful or there’s something more you’d like it to show,[let us know](https://docs.whalesync.com/resources/support) . See the[plugin’s docs](https://docs.whalesync.com/connectors/wordpress.org/whalesync-status-plugin) for the full details.
